anomalies.observed: Q1 (IRLML6402 P-MOSFET) gate is tied to GND through R5 (47k) directly, and both throws of the SPDT switch SW1 are also connected to GND (common pin 2 to the gate node, pins 1 and 3 each to a GND symbol). There is no pull-up resistor from the gate to the source (BAT) net.
anomalies.expected: The spec states SW1 is the optional power switch and that 'closing it pulls Q1's gate (through R5, 47k) low enough to turn the P-FET on and connect the battery; leaving it open keeps Q1 off and the battery disconnected.' For a high-side P-FET this requires the gate to be pulled up to the source (BAT) when the switch is open (e.g. R5 as a gate-to-source pull-up, with SW1 connecting the gate to GND only in the ON position).

evidence.quote: SW1, an SPDT switch, is the optional power switch: closing it pulls Q1's gate (through R5, 47k) low enough to turn the P-FET on and connect the battery; leaving it open keeps Q1 off and the battery disconnected.
Sheet m5-pantilt (page 1), region C: R5 47k drawn vertically from the Q1 gate node down to a GND symbol; SW_SPDT SW1 with pin 2 to the same gate node and both pin 1 and pin 3 routed to GND.

anomalies.impact: Vgs is held negative permanently, so Q1 is always ON: the battery at J5 is continuously connected to the /BAT bus pin and the optional power switch cannot disconnect it. The '(Optional) Power switch' feature is non-functional and the board can never be fully powered off from the battery.
